Anna (runtime): FYI pushed a change to the kernel scheduler yesterday that biases for bigger micro-batches to improve throughput. Seeing a small but consistent eval delta on int4+fp8 mixed runs this morning.
Raj (ml): ugh, how big is the delta and on which evals?
Anna (runtime): avg BLEU down ~1.9 on our structured-output suite (the json table tests) and a couple hallucination cases popped in the long-context chat eval. Not huge but consistent across seeds.
Marta (perf): did you correlate with perf traces? my guess is KV cache churn due to re-sharding across kernels + longer batch packing.
Anna (runtime): exactly. profiler shows spikes at kernel boundary where we evict / reload KV for several heads. see snippet:```
# timeline excerpt
kernel_switch @ 0.83s
kv_unmap @ 0.831s
kv_load @ 0.842s
recompute_attention @ 0.844s
```
Raj (ml): that timing could create slight differences in fp8 scaling when attention windows get reloaded mid-sequence -> calibration mismatch. Have you checked per-layer quant params during those windows?
Anna (runtime): quick check suggests the calibration table used for the hot-path was still the fp8-mixed profile, but because requests were split differently the effective scale selection toggled for layer 10/11 on some traces.
Leo (oncall): how reproducible locally? can we run the failing evals with server-side tracing on the dedicated cluster?
Anna (runtime): repros on dedicated-staging w/ the new scheduler flag enabled. CI perf tests didn't catch it because they use simulated steady streams, not our long-tail chat patterns.
CI-Bot: perf/run/1965432100 -> https://ci.example.com/runs/1965432100 (contains traces and compressed heap snapshots) :white_check_mark:
Marta (perf): proposal: change batching heuristic to prefer KV-affine packing -> i.e., avoid splitting tokens from the same conversation across different micro-batches unless throughput gains are > 20%. Also add small warmup window that pins KV pages for N steps when a model switches kernels.
Raj (ml): alternative: keep scheduler but add calibration stabilization step when a kernel boundary is crossed: run a tiny microstep in fp32/fp16 to prime the quant stats, then resume fp8 path. cheap but might add latency variance.
Anna (runtime): both sound reasonable. quick mitigation we can roll out: revert scheduler bias to previous behavior for the next canary, and enable "preserve_kv_locality" per-model config to opt-in for structured-output models.
Leo (oncall): agree revert for canary. can you prepare a rollback PR + per-model flag? I'll hold the canary and watch errors.
Marta (perf): I'll spike a patch that pins KV pages for 3 steps and run it on staging. If it removes the eval delta we can combine with scheduler tweaks.
Raj (ml): also run the eval suite with deterministic quant seeds and dump per-token logits for a few examples. want to see exactly where logits diverge (attention vs FFN).
Anna (runtime): done, PR #2348 created: revert scheduler bias and add preserve_kv_locality flag. Tags: @Leo, @Marta for review.
Anna (runtime): quick note: the structured-output failures are mostly truncation / malformed json objects when tokenization aligns badly after a kernel switch. that matches a tiny change in softmax dynamics when scales vary.
Marta (perf): interesting — suggests even tiny scale drift can break strict-format outputs. we should add JSON-schema checks into nightly evals to catch this earlier.
Raj (ml): agreed. I'll add a regression test that runs the schema validator with multiple quant seeds and the kv-affine scheduler variation.
Leo (oncall): timeline: revert now, run canary for 2 hours, if green merge revert into prod branch and then schedule a controlled rollout of the KV-pin approach.
Anna (runtime): will monitor. logging keys to watch: `kv_page_faults`, `kernel_switch_count`, `fp8_scale_toggles`, and `schema_validation_failures`.
CI-Bot: perf/test-suite reported one flaky json-schema fail in last 24h pre-change -> linking: https://ci.example.com/artifacts/1965400001 :eyes:
Marta (perf): ok i'll coordinate with Raj for regression test and add the small warmup in a feature branch. thanks all. :rocket:
Raj (ml): can someone capture a couple of full traces for the hallucination examples? need to inspect cross-attention weight shifts.
Anna (runtime): grabbed two dbg traces and attached to the PR. also included a minimal repro prompt.
Leo (oncall): good. keep us posted. tagging postmortem if revert fails.
Marta (perf): one more thought — consider a lightweight kernel-compatibility map so scheduler only mixes kernels when layers are quant-compatible. avoids mid-model switches for critical models.
Anna (runtime): noted. adding to follow-up items.
Anna (runtime): final: rolling revert now to canary-1. will update in ~30m with perf counters and eval run results.
